text: The assembly will now hear an address by
his excellency Mr. Danielle Roy Gil Noa
Assin, Constitutional President of the
Republic of Ecuador. I request protocol
to please escort his excellency and
invite him to address the assembly.
Secretary,
>> Secretary General of the United Nations,
Mr. President of the General Assembly,
excellencies, heads of state and
government, distinguished delegations,
ladies and gentlemen,
there was a time in which in my country,
fear prevailed over the law. This was
the experience of families that um
weren't going out at night. uh business
owners who had to pay to be able to
work, young people who were given
weapons before they were given a
diploma. We decided that this should not
be the destiny of Ecuador and we have
acted with determination. However, on
this journey, we have learned something
that I have come here to share with you.
That is that no state can defeat an
enemy that knows no borders by acting
alone.
The weapons that reach our streets cross
several countries. The money that
finances mafias is laundered far from
where the crimes are committed. The
roots of drug trafficking and people
trafficking and illegal mining cross
continents. Criminals have already
globalized their cooperation. They share
roots logistics, finances, and
technology without red tape, distrust or
delay. It's unacceptable that criminal
organizations cooperate among um with
with one another more effectively than
states do. This is the reality that the
United Nations must recognize and rise
to. For a long time, organized crime was
dealt with as a law enforcement matter.
But today, we know that it's more than
that. when uh it controls territories
and infiltrates institutions, replaces
legitimate authority, erodess the rule
of law and destabilizes entire society.
And when this happens in several
countries at the same time, it's no
longer just a domestic issue. It becomes
a threat to international peace and
security. I want to say this very
clearly. We're not calling for other
actors to act uh instead of states.
We're calling for cooperation with full
respect for the sovereignty of each
nation and with results that we can
measure.
This is why Ecuador today is proposing
three concrete actions. First of all, an
international mechanism within the
framework of the UN to trace and freeze
the illicit financial flows from
transnational organized crime. The money
is the fuel of these networks. So, let
us stop it in its tracks.
Second uh
permanent platform of information
exchange between police forces,
prosecutors offices and in financial
intelligence units that enable states to
anticipate rather than react once it's
happened. And the third concrete action
that the UN80 initiative include
transnational organized crime as a
priority for conflict prevention and
provides the organization with the
capacity to support states that request
it. These are proposals that Ecuador is
prepared to support and drive forward
alongside all countries that wish to
join us. Excellencies, security is not
an end into itself. It's a condition for
a country to be able to flourish. And
today we are experiencing a crisis, a
profound crisis. And recovering security
means
giving people back their future. for a
young person to be able to choose
university rather than being trapped by
a criminal gang. For a family to open a
business without fear, for a company to
invest and create jobs, and for
institutions to respond to the needs of
citizens and not to elicit interests.
Therefore, the success of an economy is
not measured only by how much production
grows, but rather how much it's able to
reduce poverty. is measured in um young
people with decent jobs in children with
a better education in citizens who are
able to build their future with dignity
and this also must guide the agenda of
international development. Middle inome
countries face vulnerabilities that
income per capita does not reflect.
We ask that access to cooperation and
financing be defined using more fair
vulnerability criteria and that the
international financial architecture
support the efforts of those who are
undertaking reforms. We believe in open,
predictable and equitable trade. When a
producer can export, innovate and grow,
there's a family behind that um can be
lifted out of poverty. The best social
policy is policy that generates
opportunities.
President, I come from a country that is
small in size but great, huge in terms
of our nature. The Galapicus Islands,
where Darwin uh found evidence of the
evolution of life, are a world heritage
site for the whole of humanity. And
today they are threatened by illegal
fishing networks that operate with the
same logic and the same financing of
other organized crime groups. Uh the
same is happening with illegal mining in
the Amazon that's destroying forests and
funding gangs. Protecting nature is also
a matter of security. Ecuador will uh
continue to fulfill our responsibilities
and invites all of you to join to join
us. Latin America and the Caribbean is a
region with a lot of talent talent,
energy, food, strategic resources, and
above all uh youth that has resolved to
building a different future. It's a
region that um has not come to this
assembly to ask for uh solutions from
the outside but rather to offer up our
solutions and one with the greatest um
one of the greatest challenges of the
future is artificial intelligence. It
can transform education, multiply
productivity and close historic gaps but
um also entrench inequalities and serve
those that seek to weaken our
institutions. We need international
governance that enables us to innovate
without renouncing our values and that
does not leave those that have the least
resources behind. Um they also need to
be able to access this technology.
Excellencies, um confidence in the
multilateral system is going through
difficult times. Many citizens see a
gulf between what we agree on here and
what people experience on a daily basis.
Closing this gap is the task of our
organization. A lot of um citizens
um realize that um this is the task that
our generation must take up. And as a
founding country, Ecuador believes in
the United Nations. And it's it's
precisely for this reason that we want
an organization that's able to respond
to the challenges of the world today,
not of 1945.
supporting the organization that the
United Nations also needs to involve um
a willingness to transform the United
Nations and that's why we support the UN
initiative and um pose an essential
question. What United Nations does the
world need today? Um we need an
organization that's more efficient with
the ability to prevent conflicts,
resolve crises, and support states to
challenges that didn't exist when the
organization was created. an
organization whose legitimacy depends
not only on the decision that we adopt
but the way that they adopt. And we need
the charter and international law to
remain our common language. More than 80
years ago, countries understood that
peace didn't depend on um everyone's
power, but rather um is something that
um we built organizations to cooperate
to achieve. This remains our main
strength. The citizens of the world will
not judge this organization by its
declarations. They will judge it by its
ability to turn commitments into peace
and security, into respect for human
rights, into real opportunities for
development, and how many lives we
really save. President, the criminal
gangs already coordinate with each
other. Now we need to do better. Ecuador
has come to this assembly to defend
collector solutions because no country
can build a safe, prosperous and
sustainable future alone and because
when international cooperation works,
we are all stronger for it. Thank you
very much.
On behalf of the assembly, I wish to
thank the constitutional president of
the Republic of Ecuador.
